WHAT_WAS_WRONG.claim_as_published: 'Exactly 5 DAILY slots missed 07-20, all 5 in 00:30-04:00 GMT+7. Band-shaped, not slot-shaped.'
WHAT_WAS_WRONG.error_1_count: WRONG. >=7 slots missed, not 5. bctc-analyst-slot-1 (15:00Z) and slot-4 (00:00Z) also missed and were invisible to my query.
WHAT_WAS_WRONG.error_2_shape: WRONG. Not a band. The session was alive ~07:15-11:15 Paris on 07-20 and dead from ~11:15 onward through the night. Loss starts mid-DAY, not in unattended overnight hours.
WHAT_WAS_WRONG.error_3_timezone: WRONG CLOCK. I converted to GMT+7 because user memory records GMT+7 — but that is the VN MARKET timezone. The host is Europe/Paris (CEST, UTC+2, verified via readlink /etc/localtime). Every local time in the original finding is 5 hours off.

CORRECTED_FINDING.so_what: ALL FOUR bctc passes were lost on 07-20, plus the chef evening dish, digest, and the TNB audit. That is a materially bigger loss than the original finding reported, and it reframes the fix: the exposure window opens when a laptop closes at midday, not at some overnight boundary. OPS-COWORK-GUARANTEED-SLOT-INSTALL [REVIEW] is worth more than my first number implied.

HOW_I_GOT_IT_WRONG_methodological.root_cause: I concluded from whichever single evidence plane I had just queried, and published before triangulating. Three planes, two of which CANNOT answer this question:
HOW_I_GOT_IT_WRONG_methodological.plane_1_last_fired_CANNOT: Single scalar, self-erasing. slot-1 and slot-4 fired again on 07-21 and overwrote their own 07-20 evidence. This is why I saw 5 instead of 7.
HOW_I_GOT_IT_WRONG_methodological.plane_2_git_log_census_CANNOT: git log --name-only misses UNTRACKED files entirely. The chef synthesis JSONs and fb-post-2026-07-20.md that disprove my second hypothesis were sitting untracked on disk, invisible to every git query I ran. A git census measures COMMIT activity, not AGENT activity, and in this repo those diverge badly.
HOW_I_GOT_IT_WRONG_methodological.plane_3_filesystem_CAN: find docs -name '*2026-07-20*' -o -name '*20260720*'. Dated output artifacts are per-run and non-overwriting, so they are the only durable per-day record of what executed. This should have been the FIRST query; it would have given the right answer in one step.
HOW_I_GOT_IT_WRONG_methodological.the_caveat_that_did_not_save_me: My original finding contained a correctly-worded caveat ('5 is a LOWER BOUND, not a census; last_fired is a single scalar'). I wrote the true caveat and a false headline in the same document and shipped both. A disclosed limitation does not protect a reader who is handed an overclaiming headline next to it. If the evidence supports only a lower bound, the HEADLINE must state the bound.
HOW_I_GOT_IT_WRONG_methodological.for_po: Treat this as a process finding about me, not only a data correction. No row requested.
